purpose: Define the epistemic meaning, minimum evidence, and permitted transitions for continuity claims without storing private source material.

observed.definition: Directly supported by an inspectable source or runtime artifact available to the current run.
minimum_evidence: A stable source identifier or repository path.
A bounded description of what the source actually establishes.
No stronger conclusion than the source supports.
prohibited_shortcuts: Treating a committed workflow as proof that the workflow ran.
Treating a fixture result as truth of the underlying real-world claim.

inferred.definition: A conclusion derived from one or more observed claims through an explicit reasoning step.
minimum_evidence: At least one observed supporting claim.
The inference rule or reasoning bridge is stated.
Plausible alternatives are not silently excluded.
prohibited_shortcuts: Relabeling an inference as observed because it is highly plausible.
Using private source content when a bounded provenance reference is sufficient.

proposed.definition: A candidate interpretation, structure, test, or future project decision that has not yet been accepted as project state.
minimum_evidence: The proposal is clearly separated from current state.
An acceptance, falsification, or decision route is named.
prohibited_shortcuts: Writing a proposal as though it were already implemented or agreed.
Using a proposal to overwrite contradictory observed history.

superseded.definition: A formerly active claim or decision that has been replaced while its historical provenance remains preserved.
minimum_evidence: Identifier of the replacing claim or decision.
prohibited_shortcuts: Deleting or rewriting the prior claim.
Marking a contradiction as superseded without a replacement decision.

unresolved.definition: A material question, contradiction, evidence gap, or verification step that remains open.
minimum_evidence: The missing evidence or decision is named.
The next feasible resolution route is stated when known.
prohibited_shortcuts: Converting absence of evidence into evidence of absence.
Closing the item solely because a tool or provider was temporarily unavailable.

permitted_transitions.condition: Implementation or decision acceptance is directly evidenced; the observation must describe only the evidenced event, not the truth of every premise behind it.
A different proposal or decision replaces it and the replacement is identified.
The missing source, runtime artifact, or decision becomes inspectable.
The observation represented mutable project state that was later replaced; the historical event itself remains observed.
New direct evidence independently establishes the same bounded claim.
New evidence or a stronger inference replaces it while preserving the prior reasoning record.

forbidden_transitions.reason: An unresolved question cannot be retired without a replacement, explicit cancellation decision, or evidence that it is no longer material.
Direct evidence may support additional inferences, but the observed record must not be downgraded or rewritten.
A superseded claim may remain historically observed, but reactivation requires a new claim identifier and new evidence.

non_equivalence_rules: repository implementation is not runtime execution
runtime execution is not deployment verification
deployment verification is not scientific or medical truth
synthetic fixture validity is not truth of private memory content
peer trigger attempt is not peer execution

allowed: Repository paths and immutable commit identifiers.
Hashed or bounded provenance references that do not expose private content.
disallowed: Private health, identity, relationship, or location narratives.
Secret values, access tokens, or provider credentials.
A source quotation when a bounded provenance reference is sufficient.

compatibility.claim_transition_contract: This lexicon narrows interpretation of claim states; it does not replace the append-only claim transition contract or its validator.
compatibility.canonical_queue: This artifact does not alter another team's canonical queue item.
